headline: High-risk shared-git workflow: Aider can write/commit repo state while pdf.js reads browser-rendered PDFs, creating medium prompt-injection and data-leakage exposure with low direct compliance risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read/write the shared git repo and auto-commit changes; pdf.js processes PDF files in a browser-based worker. If PDF content is copied into the repo or Aider ingests pdf.js output, malicious document text can steer Aider. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not default-manual only.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is pasted or written into the shared repo and Aider reads it as instructions
IF the PDF contains attacker-controlled prompt text that survives into Aider's context
mitigations: Keep pdf.js outputs in a separate non-repo folder
Require manual review before Aider edits any file derived from PDFs
Prefix imported PDF text as untrusted data in notes
Use a throwaway branch for PDF-derived work
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between PDF extraction and code editing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and has broad network egress; pdf.js touches PDF documents and files. If the shared repo contains sensitive PDFs or extracted text, Aider can read them and potentially send context to configured model providers. The pair does not show an isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default repo-sharing workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs or extracted text are stored in the shared repository
IF Aider sends repo context to a configured external model provider
mitigations: Store sensitive PDFs outside the shared repo
Disable or restrict external model providers for sensitive sessions
Use a separate repo for document processing
Review git diffs before commit
requires-engineering: enforce file-level access controls between code and PDF workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, while pdf.js reads PDF files and supports multiple instances. Because Aider shares state via a git repo and can mutate it, concurrent edits can collide with PDF-derived artifacts or annotations. The overlap is on the same mutable workspace, and no locking is documented, so default collaboration is dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF pdf.js-derived files are edited while Aider is committing changes
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Keep PDF artifacts in a different directory
Run a quick git status before each commit
requires-engineering: add workspace locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code changes and commits, while pdf.js can produce extracted document content. If pdf.js output is treated as authoritative input to Aider without verification, errors or malicious text can cascade into committed repository changes. The pair lacks a built-in verification step between document extraction and code editing.
conditions: IF extracted PDF text is fed into Aider as facts or instructions
IF Aider commits changes based on unverified document output
mitigations: Require a human check of extracted text before editing
Compare PDF text against the source PDF for key claims
Limit Aider to draft-only mode for document-derived tasks
Keep a changelog of source claims versus code edits
requires-engineering: add automated verification between extraction and commit

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history, while pdf.js handles PDF documents. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so only a narrow compliance concern exists if regulated PDFs are placed into the shared repo and then processed by Aider. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same files.
conditions: IF regulated or personal PDFs are stored in the shared repository
IF Aider's external model provider receives those files or their extracted text
mitigations: Keep regulated PDFs out of the code repo
Use local-only models for regulated material
Delete extracted text after review
Restrict repo access to authorized staff
requires-engineering: document retention and residency controls
